## Where the classifier reads configuration

The classifier reads the same [CLAUDE.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md) content Claude itself loads, so an instruction like "never force push" in your project's CLAUDE.md steers both Claude and the classifier at the same time. Start there for project conventions and behavioral rules.

For rules that apply across projects, such as trusted infrastructure or organization-wide deny rules, use the `autoMode` settings block. The classifier reads `autoMode` from the following scopes:

| Scope | File | Use for |
| :- | :- | :- |
| One developer | `~/.claude/settings.json` | Personal trusted infrastructure |
| Organization-wide | [Managed settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings.md) | Trusted infrastructure distributed to all developers |
| `--settings` flag or Agent SDK | Inline JSON | Per-invocation overrides for automation |

The classifier doesn't read `autoMode` from project settings in `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`. Both files live in the repo directory, so a checked-in repo or a build step could otherwise inject its own allow rules. Move any `autoMode` block in `.claude/settings.local.json` to `~/.claude/settings.json`.

Entries from each scope are combined. A developer can extend `environment`, `allow`, `soft_deny`, and `hard_deny` with personal entries but can't remove entries that managed settings provide. Because allow rules act as exceptions to soft block rules inside the classifier, a developer-added `allow` entry can override an organization `soft_deny` entry: the combination is additive, not a hard policy boundary.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The classifier is a second gate that runs after the [permissions system](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md). For actions that must never run regardless of user intent or classifier configuration, use `permissions.deny` in managed settings, which blocks the action before the classifier is consulted and can't be overridden.

>
> * `soft_deny`: every built-in soft block rule, including force push, `curl | bash`, production deploys, and auto-mode bypass
> * `hard_deny`: the built-in data exfiltration rule

Each section is evaluated independently, so setting `environment` alone leaves the default `allow`, `soft_deny`, and `hard_deny` lists intact.

Only omit `"$defaults"` when you intend to take full ownership of the list. To do that safely, run `claude auto-mode defaults` to print the built-in rules, copy them into your settings file, then review each rule against your own pipeline and risk tolerance.

### `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`

Block CLI startup until Claude Code has freshly fetched [server-managed settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings.md). If the fetch fails, Claude Code exits instead of continuing with cached or no settings. Set it when your environment can't accept even a brief window in which a session runs without its managed policy.

When the key is unset, Claude Code doesn't block startup on the fetch, though when the developer signs in at startup it waits up to five seconds for the fetch. [Anthropic can require the settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings.md#fetch-and-caching-behavior), which does block a start without them. A Cloud gateway session waits, and exits if the gateway can't be reached.

* **Scope**: [`Managed`](#scopes). Claude Code honors a `true` from any admin-controlled managed source, even one that isn't the highest-priority source.
* **Type**: Boolean
  * `true`: Claude Code blocks startup until it has freshly fetched server-managed settings, and exits if the fetch fails
  * `false`: unless Anthropic requires the settings, Claude Code doesn't block startup on the fetch, though at a sign-in startup it waits up to five seconds for the fetch
* **Default**: `false`

```json managed-settings.json theme={null}
{
  "forceRemoteSettingsRefresh": true
### `cleanupPeriodDays`

Set how many days Claude Code keeps [session transcripts and other application data](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory.md#cleaned-up-automatically) before deleting them. Claude Code runs the deletion as a background sweep after a session starts, as long as it can safely determine the retention period. The sweep deletes transcripts without showing a message, so a session you haven't used for longer than the retention period no longer appears in the [`/resume`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions#resume-a-session) picker.

* **Scope**: [`Any file`](#scopes)
* **Type**: number of days, a whole number, minimum `1`
* **Default**: `30`

```json settings.json theme={null}
### `sandbox.network.allowLocalBinding`

Let sandboxed commands on macOS listen on network ports, for example to start a dev server, and connect to any port on localhost. A command that listens on a non-loopback address accepts connections from other machines. The key has no effect on Linux and WSL2, where each sandboxed command has its own loopback interface. To reach a server on the host from Linux or WSL2, see [A command fails to reach a server on localhost](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md#a-command-fails-to-reach-a-server-on-localhost).

* **Scope**: [`Any file`](#scopes), with [limits on project and local settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md#repository-settings-under-an-admin-required-sandbox)
* **Type**: Boolean
  * `true`: sandboxed commands on macOS can listen on any local address and connect to any port on localhost
  * `false`: sandboxed commands on macOS can't listen on a port or connect directly to servers on localhost
* **Default**: `false`

### Enforce fail-closed startup

By default, if the remote settings fetch fails at startup, the CLI continues with the settings cached from the last successful fetch. The [values Claude Code withholds](#fetch-and-caching-behavior) stay withheld until a fetch succeeds. On a machine that has never fetched them, the CLI continues without server-managed settings and still applies any [endpoint-managed settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md#delivery-mechanisms) on the device. [Anthropic can require the settings](#fetch-and-caching-behavior) instead.

To stop clients from starting on cached or absent server-managed settings, set `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh: true` in your managed settings.

Clients signed in through a [Claude apps gateway](#platform-availability) wait for the startup fetch whether or not you set this, and handle a failed fetch as follows:

* If the gateway answers an attended interactive launch with a `401` and this setting is off, the gateway has ended that sign-in. Claude Code prints [`Cloud gateway session expired — run /login to reconnect.`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors#cloud-gateway-session-expired) and opens the session signed out of the gateway until the user runs `/login`.
* When the fetch fails in any other way, or in any other kind of launch except a `claude auth` subcommand, the client exits with an error.

When this setting is active in a session that fetches server-managed settings, the CLI blocks at startup until remote settings are freshly fetched. If the fetch fails, the CLI exits rather than proceeding without the policy. This setting self-perpetuates: once delivered from the server, it is also cached locally so that subsequent startups enforce the same behavior even before the first successful fetch of a new session. A session that [doesn't fetch server-managed settings](#platform-availability) starts without waiting.

To enable this, add the key to your managed settings configuration:

## Layer 4 — Supply chain for MCP servers and plugins

**Principle.** Local MCP servers, plugins and hooks run with the engineer's access (📖 R1.6.2, R5.5.5); remote MCP servers receive tokens and data.
Only reviewed, pinned entries from a catalogue are allowed. The catalogue is the inventory (P4c).
Review takes ≤ 5 working days (S6), or people work around it.

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Plugins:** a private marketplace repo with `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (📖 R1.4.1), sources
  pinned to `ref`/`sha` (📖 R1.4.1b, link only). Managed `strictKnownMarketplaces` = Papaya only,
  `blockedMarketplaces`, `enabledPlugins: false` to pull one (📖 R1.4.2), checked before download and
  at session start (📖 R1.4.3). `disableSideloadFlags` rejects `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`,
  `--agents`, `--mcp-config` but not `.mcp.json` or `claude mcp add` (📖 R1.4.2). With
  `allowManagedHooksOnly`, plugin hooks run only for force-enabled plugins (📖 R1.5.4). User mods are
  blocked by the `allowManagedModsOnly` option under `pluginConfigs` → `cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin`
  → `options` (📖 R1.5.6). The version floor covers the plugin-pin fix of 2.1.179 (📖 R6.2.7).
- **MCP:** "approved catalogue" = `allowedMcpServers` + `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true`; without
  the lock users can widen it (📖 R1.3.1, R1.3.4). Match by `serverUrl` or `serverCommand`, never
  `serverName` ("not a security control", 📖 R1.3.3); `serverCommand` matches the exact argv (📖 R1.3.3), so the catalogue entry pins an exact package version in it [design].
  `disableClaudeAiConnectors: true` (📖 R1.3.7). With MDM, `managed-mcp.json` gives exclusive control;
  it cannot come from server-managed settings (📖 R1.3.2).
- **Review checklist** [design]: publisher; local `stdio` or remote (📖 R6.4.3); what it reads and where
  it sends data, with a supplier-register entry and BAA/DPA status (⚠️ R5.6); no token passthrough
  (📖 R6.4.2); write tools for Slack, Linear, GitHub only where needed (⚠️ R6.5 #6); how the server authenticates (Linear and Slack: G9); pinned version,
  reviewer, date.
- **Known gaps:** no per-group targeting in server-managed settings (📖 R1.1.6, R1.4.4); tool
  description changes after approval are not covered (⚠️ research 6.6).

**Audit evidence.** Catalogue file in git (each entry = an approved PR); supplier register; OTel
`claude_code.plugin_installed` / `plugin_loaded` (📖 R1.4.6). MCP tool logging needs
`OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1` (📖 R1.3.8); it stays off until we know whether it logs tool inputs (⚠️).

**Cost / value.** Up to 5 days' wait for a new tool. Compliance gets an asset inventory and supplier
records.

To require that developers' claude.ai logins belong to a specific Anthropic organization, set [`forceLoginMethod`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#forceloginmethod) and [`forceLoginOrgUUID`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#forceloginorguuid) in [managed settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md). Set `forceLoginOrgUUID` to your organization ID, shown in [claude.ai admin settings](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/organization) for Claude for Teams or Enterprise organizations. Claude Code reports an error for a claude.ai login to any other organization and exits at startup if the claude.ai credential in use belongs to an organization that isn't listed.

For Claude Console logins, Claude Code uses `forceLoginOrgUUID` to pre-select the organization on the Console sign-in page when you set it to a single Console organization ID, shown at [platform.claude.com/settings/organization](https://platform.claude.com/settings/organization). It doesn't check which organization the resulting Console credential belongs to, at login or at startup. A developer who logged in with a Console account before you deployed the keys stays logged in, and that saved key is blocked on a machine that also requires the [gateway](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway) sign-in or in a session that selects a cloud provider.

If you set `forceLoginOrgUUID` in any settings file, Claude Code stops offering the [keyless Console sign-in](#sign-in-without-an-api-key) in the sessions that file applies to and creates an API key instead. To direct developers to claude.ai sign-in instead, set `forceLoginMethod` to `"claudeai"`.

On Claude Code v2.1.212 or later, every login path listed here applies `forceLoginMethod`. On the terminal's interactive login screen, reached by `/login` or first-run onboarding, Claude Code pre-selects a `claudeai` or `console` method without enforcing it, so even with `forceLoginMethod` set to `"claudeai"`, a developer can still complete a Console login there.

The paths differ on `forceLoginOrgUUID`:

* **Terminal, [VS Code extension](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code.md), and Agent SDK logins**: verify `forceLoginOrgUUID` for claude.ai account logins
* **`claude setup-token` and `/install-github-app`**: enforce only `forceLoginMethod`, so they can mint a token in a different organization
* **[Gateway](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway) sign-in**: selected by `forceLoginMethod: "gateway"` rather than restricted by it, and doesn't authenticate against an Anthropic organization, so `forceLoginOrgUUID` doesn't apply; use your gateway identity provider to restrict access

Deploy `forceLoginMethod` and `forceLoginOrgUUID` through your device management tooling. A developer receives [server-managed settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings.md) only after authenticating into your organization, so you can't redirect a first login with those settings. If you also distribute server-managed settings from claude.ai, set both keys there too until every client runs v2.1.299 or later. For where to set the keys afterward, and which source's value applies, see [Which managed source supplies login keys](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings.md#which-managed-source-supplies-login-keys).

In a [gateway](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway) deployment, also keep `forceLoginMethod` and `forceLoginOrgUUID` out of the [settings the gateway serves](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway-config.md#managed).

The keys also decide whether a session that doesn't use a login credential can start. See [`forceLoginOrgUUID`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#forceloginorguuid) in the settings reference for the full behavior.

* **`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper`**: blocked at startup. Under `forceLoginOrgUUID`, organization membership can't be verified for an environment credential, and under `forceLoginMethod` the credential would stand in for the required sign-in. When the managed settings also require the [gateway](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway) sign-in, Claude Code blocks an API key saved by an earlier Claude Console login the same way. See [Administrator policy requires a Cloud gateway sign-in](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md#administrator-policy-requires-a-cloud-gateway-sign-in)
* **Cloud provider sessions such as Amazon Bedrock**: blocked only while an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper` credential, or an API key saved by an earlier Claude Console login, is still present on the machine. Remove it and the session starts. These sessions authenticate against your cloud provider, whose access policies govern them
* **[Anthropic profile or federation credentials](#anthropic-profiles-and-federation-credentials)**: not blocked unless an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper` credential, or an API key saved by an earlier Claude Console login, is also present on the machine. The keys don't check which organization the profile belongs to

content.content:
### Executables

Files in `bin/` at the plugin root are on the `PATH` of the Bash tool's shell while the plugin is enabled, so Claude can run them as bare commands. A command that Claude runs with the [PowerShell tool](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference.md#powershell-tool) outside the [sandbox](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md) finds them on its `PATH` too, and a sandboxed PowerShell command doesn't. Add an executable script:

```bash bin/hello-plugin theme={null}
#!/bin/bash
echo "hello from my-plugin"
```

Make it executable with `chmod +x bin/hello-plugin` and load the plugin. When you ask Claude to run `hello-plugin`, the Bash tool result shows the script's output.

Plugin `bin/` directories come after the user's own `PATH` entries, so a plugin can't shadow `git`, `ls`, or another system command.

claude.ai and Cowork don't install a plugin that has a top-level `bin/` directory, including one you [distribute through claude.ai organization settings](https://claude.com/docs/plugins/org-sync#keep-executables-out-of-the-top-level-bin-directory).

### Default settings

To set defaults that apply while the plugin is enabled, add a `settings.json` at the plugin root, or put the same object inline in the `settings` manifest key. Two keys take effect, `agent` and `subagentStatusLine`, and every other key is dropped.

Set `agent` to run one of the plugin's own agents as the main thread:

```json settings.json theme={null}
{
  "agent": "security-reviewer"
}
```

Load the plugin and start a session. Claude then answers in the main conversation with the `security-reviewer` agent's system prompt and model.

For everything the key controls, see the [`agent` setting](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#agent).

When the same key is set in more than one place, these rules decide which value applies:

* **File over manifest**: when both exist and `settings.json` sets at least one supported key, `settings.json` applies and the manifest's `settings` is ignored
* **User settings over plugin defaults**: across settings sources, plugin defaults are the lowest layer, so a user's own `agent` in `~/.claude/settings.json` overrides yours
* **Two plugins set the same key**: the value from the plugin loaded last applies, and `claude --debug` logs `overrides setting`

For the `subagentStatusLine` shape, see [subagent status lines](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline.md#subagent-status-lines).

### Monitors

A monitor is a shell command that runs in the background for the whole session. What it prints reaches Claude as notifications, so Claude can react to a log or a status change without being asked to watch it. Save the entries in `monitors/monitors.json`:

```json monitors/monitors.json theme={null}
[
  {
    "name": "error-log",
    "command": "tail -F ./logs/error.log",
    "description": "Application error log"
  }
]

# Step 3 review, round 2 (E8–E10): independent reviewer report

**Scope:** the step-3 files listed in the brief. I did not edit any repo file. `git status --short` at the end is identical to the snapshot taken at session start.

**What I ran, all in `/tmp/claude-1001/-home-do-hoang-minh-hung-papaya-devsecops-challenge/6db3dd9e-1a2b-4563-ab89-a7de7a1f8366/scratchpad/review-s3r2/`:**
- **Docs:** fetched the docs (settings-reference, sandboxing, permissions, permission-modes, auto-mode-config, iam, managed-settings, server-managed-settings, plugins/marketplace-reference, plugins/org, plugins/components, plugins/mods/admin, vs-code) and the HIPAA template plus its README into `docs/`.
- **Template commit:** the GitHub API shows the latest commit touching `settings-hipaa.json` is `9196319` (2026-10-08). This matches the README.
- **validate.sh:** ran it on a copy in `ex/` and got "RESULT: all executed checks passed": 27/27 policy cases and 105 unit tests.
- **Mutations:** `scripts/mut.py` and `scripts/mut2.py` mutate the copy. Each mutation targets one property, and I removed the cases where a different test was the one failing.
- **Policy probes:** `pp/probe.ts`, compiled against the real `@pulumi/aws` 7.51.1, `@pulumi/policy` v1.21.0 and TypeScript 6.0.3.
- **`claude plugin validate`** (2.1.319) on a mutated marketplace copy:
  - unpinned `github` → passed (exit 0)
  - malformed `sha` → failed (exit 1)
  - `npm` `x@latest` → passed (exit 0)

  This matches the README.

**Checked and correct (✅/📖):**
- Every key in both files exists in settings-reference. The version floors hold: `allowedProviders` 2.1.285, `classifyAllShell` 2.1.193, `blockedMarketplaces` 2.1.223, `crossSessionInbound` 2.1.224/2.1.232, `credentials.files` 2.1.221, `requiredMinimumVersion` 2.1.163.
- `pluginConfigs["cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin"].options.allowManagedModsOnly` matches mods/admin.md, which says "The id has one form here".
- The `excludedCommands` matching rules in finding 22 match sandboxing.md.
- `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` requires 2.1.257.
- Read deny rules cover `cat`/`head`/`tail` (permissions.md L354).
- The `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` and MDM-first-login claims are right.
- The built-in MCP servers are exempt from the allowlist.
- All 15 `@pulumi/aws` type tokens used exist. The real `isTypeOf` in server.js compares `__pulumiType` the same way the test stub does.
- Unknown values fall back to `advisory` (server.js L287–290).

---

## HIGH

None.

---

## MEDIUM

### M1. Phase 2 drops the template's `autoMode` `"$defaults"` pins, and the README gives a wrong reason

**Where:** `managed-settings.phase2.json:10-12`; `README.md:109` ("Unset is the default; only `classifyAllShell: true` is kept").

**Evidence:**
- README-hipaa.md ("Auto mode"): "The file pins `"$defaults"` in `environment`, `soft_deny`, and `hard_deny`, so a developer's own list adds to the built-in entries and can't replace them."
- auto-mode-config.md L74: "can't remove entries that managed settings provide".
- auto-mode-config.md L267–270: "Setting any of … `soft_deny`, or `hard_deny` without `"$defaults"` replaces the entire default list … `soft_deny`: every built-in soft block rule, including force push, `curl | bash`, production deploys … `hard_deny`: the built-in data exfiltration rule".
- Mutation: `autoMode.hard_deny: []` → the tests still pass.

**Effect:** With the pins unset, a `soft_deny`/`hard_deny` list in a developer's `~/.claude/settings.json` or `--settings` throws away the built-in rules. That includes the exfiltration rule. Auto mode stays available (D1), and in auto mode the classifier is often the only gate. The deviation is presented as a no-op, but it removes a lock.

**Fix:** Keep the three pins exactly as the template has them. This costs nothing. Add a test that each list contains `"$defaults"`. Alternatively, record it as a real deviation and state its effect.

### M2. `pulumi *` and `serverless *` exclusions reopen every credential the sandbox hides; the README says "each one prompts"

**Where:**
- `managed-settings.phase2.json:135-139`
- `README.md:62` ("excluded (they prompt)")
- `README.md:308-312` (finding 20)
- `README.md:322` ("so each one prompts")
- `tests/test_claude_settings.py:203-204`

**Evidence:**
- sandboxing.md, `excludedCommands` warning: "If you write a pattern that covers an interpreter, a script inside your working directory, or a tool that acts on a file there, as `docker compose` does with its compose file, Claude can write that file and then run it outside the sandbox."
- sandboxing.md: "An excluded command goes through the regular permission flow: … In auto mode, the classifier reviews other excluded commands."

**Effect:** OD12 auto-allows sandboxed commands, so a sandboxed command can write `index.ts` or `serverless.yml` in the repo with no prompt. `pulumi preview` then runs that code outside the sandbox: it can read `~/.config/gh`, `~/.ssh` and `~/.aws`, and the network is unrestricted.
- In Manual mode, the only prompt says `pulumi preview`.
- In auto mode, the classifier decides and nobody is asked.

So finding 20's claim (hiding `~/.config/gh` stops the agent approving PRs as the engineer) and the test comment are overstated, and "each one prompts" is wrong for auto mode. Framework layer 2 L211–222 already accepts this risk for `~/.aws`, but the E8 row, finding 20 and finding 22 do not carry it over.

**Fix:**
- State this limit in E8 "does not prove", finding 20 and finding 22.
- Fix "each one prompts" to "prompts in Manual mode; in auto mode the classifier decides".
- Option, with cost: add `permissions.ask: ["WebFetch", "Bash(aws *)", "Bash(pulumi *)", "Bash(serverless *)"]`. permission-modes.md L329 says "Explicit ask rules still force a prompt" in auto mode, so a person approves every unsandboxed run. The cost is a prompt per `aws` call in auto mode too.

### M3. The phase-2 sandbox read scope is a denylist; `allowManagedReadPathsOnly` does nothing here and would cancel `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories`

**Where:** `managed-settings.phase2.json:140-166` and `318-329`; `README.md:112` and `308`.

**Evidence:**
- sandboxing.md: by default sandboxed reads cover "Most of the machine".
- settings-reference.md L1541ff: `allowManagedReadPathsOnly` only filters `allowRead`. The docs' example pairs it with `"denyRead": ["~/"]` and `"allowRead": ["~/work"]`. Phase 2 sets neither, so the key has no effect.
- settings-reference.md L1083–1085: the sandbox half of `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` "doesn't reach sandboxed commands" when "`allowManagedReadPathsOnly` is set". Finding 19 proposes that key, so adopting it later would silently do nothing for sandboxed commands.
- Egress, sandboxing.md "Security limitations": "Allowing broad domains such as `github.com` can create paths for data exfiltration … domain fronting".
- Egress, README-hipaa.md: "a sandboxed command can send data to any allowlisted host, including other repositories on the same Git host".
- Mutation: adding `"*"` or `"*.amazonaws.com"` to `allowedDomains` → the tests still pass.

**Effect:** Sandboxed commands can read everything in home that is not on the list, with no prompt, and send it to `github.com`, npm or PyPI, for example a push to another repository using a token the attacker supplies. Credentials in Papaya's stack that the list misses (⚠️ paths not checked):
- Serverless Framework v4: `~/.serverlessrc` and `SERVERLESS_ACCESS_KEY`
- `PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE`
- key files that `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` or `KUBECONFIG` point to outside the denied folders
- Linear and Slack tokens

So "credential denies for the whole stack" (README:62) is overstated. None of this is stated in E8.

**Fix:**
- Either use the docs' pattern `denyRead: ["~/"]` plus `allowRead` for the workspace roots (cost: Papaya must fix where repos live, e.g. `~/src`), or drop `allowManagedReadPathsOnly` if `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` is preferred.
- State the egress-through-allowed-domains limit in E8.
- Add a test that `allowedDomains` contains no `*` entry.

### M4. Settings that break normal engineering work, with the cost not stated

**Where:** `README.md:114-117` (the costs paragraph names only `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`, `allowLocalBinding`, `cleanupPeriodDays` and `gh`); `SKILL.md:11-12`.

**Evidence:**
- README-hipaa.md, "What developers lose": private npm registries fail, `/goal` is gone under `allowManagedHooksOnly`.
- README-hipaa.md, "Check a computer" step 3: "`git` against a private repository can still fail to sign in, because the file hides SSH keys, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.netrc`, the GitHub token variables, and the `gh` configuration".
- sandboxing.md: git over SSH fails on macOS; Go CLIs fail TLS on macOS; Unix sockets such as Docker's are not allowed (`allowAllUnixSockets: false`).
- settings-reference.md: `allowLocalBinding: false` also blocks connecting to servers on localhost on macOS.
- sandboxing.md L13: the sandbox does not run on native Windows, so with `failIfUnavailable` Claude Code does not start there.

**Effect:** Inside the sandbox, `git fetch`, `git pull` and `git push` to the private monorepo fail, as do private-scope `npm ci`, Docker and Testcontainers, and local database tests on macOS. The prod-change skill tells the agent to "open a pull request", but it can neither push nor run `gh` from the sandbox.

**Fix:** List these in the costs paragraph, with the workaround (`!` prompt). Note the native-Windows effect.

### M5. The wildcard rule can be evaded with `?` forms that mean the same as `*` or `<service>:*`

**Where:** `pulumi-policy/policies.ts:31-43`.

**Evidence (probe output):**
- `"s3:?*"` → `[]`
- `"ec2:**"` → `[]`
- `"*?"` → `[]`
- `"iam:?*"` → flagged, because only identity services are checked for any wildcard

IAM supports `?` in action names (⚠️ from memory; the IAM doc was not fetched). Under that reading, `s3:?*` grants every S3 action.

**Effect:** A mandatory policy meant to compensate for OD8 is passed by an equivalent spelling.

**Fix:** Treat an action as a full wildcard when the whole action, or the part after `:`, matches `^[*?]+$`. Add the three cases above to the tests.

---

## LOW

### L1. README E10 (`README.md:64`): "by any route" is overstated

Probes, all returning `[]`:
- `aws:ssoadmin/managedPolicyAttachment` with `AdministratorAccess`
- `aws:ssoadmin/permissionSetInlinePolicy` with `"*"`
- `AdministratorAccess-Amplify` (admin-equivalent names that are neither `AdministratorAccess` nor `*FullAccess`)
- `aws:s3/accountPublicAccessBlock` with a flag off
- `aws:rds/instance` and `aws:rds/globalCluster` without deletion protection

Framework L510–512 says policy packs do not apply to Serverless stacks, but E10's limits column does not say so.

**Fix:** Name the routes that are covered instead of "any route". Add the ssoadmin types, or state them as not covered. Add the Serverless limit to E10.

### L2. Tests don't pin several stated properties (mutations that still pass)

- **Phase 2, still passing after mutation:**
  - all `Edit(...)` denies removed
  - `denyWrite` emptied
  - `forceLoginMethod` removed
  - `allowedHttpHookUrls: ["*"]`
  - `skillOverrides` removed
  - `cleanupPeriodDays: 3650`
- **Both phases:**
  - MCP `serverCommand` `["npx","-y","evil@latest","x@1.0.0"]` passes, because the regex matches any pinned argument
  - `serverUrl: "https://*"` passes
- **Marketplace:**
  - npm `package: "x@latest"` with a decoy `version` passes. The docs say `version` is used only "when `package` is a package name with no version appended".
  - an npm tarball URL passes
  - a foreign `registry` passes

So E9's claim "every external source is pinned (… exact npm version …)" is overstated.

**Fix:**
- MCP: check the package argument itself.
- npm: reject `@` after the name and `https:` packages; decide on `registry`.
- Add asserts for the remaining keys, or say they are untested.

### L3. The deviation table's "added" row (`README.md:112`) lists template keys as additions

It lists `allowedProviders`, `forceLoginMethod`, `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, `allowManagedHooksOnly`, `allowedHttpHookUrls`, `disableSideloadFlags`, and `sandbox.enabled`/`failIfUnavailable`/`allowUnsandboxedCommands`. All of these are in the template (diffed). The row also leaves out `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed: true` (OD12), which the template does not set. The E8 row (`README:62`) likewise presents template keys as "Papaya's deviations".

**Fix:** Regenerate the row from a diff against the template.

### L4. Two README claims go further than the docs

- **`forceLoginMethod: claudeai` ("no Console API-key login"), `README:112`.** iam.md L178: "On the terminal's interactive login screen … Claude Code pre-selects a `claudeai` or `console` method without enforcing it, so even with `forceLoginMethod` set to `"claudeai"`, a developer can still complete a Console login there." `allowedProviders: ["anthropic"]` also admits Console sign-ins. A Console sign-in could therefore send data to a non-Papaya organisation. Framework layer 2 only partly covers this.
- **`allowedHttpHookUrls: []` ("no HTTP hook may send data out").** README-hipaa.md: "`allowedHttpHookUrls` … also take entries from a developer's own settings … `allowManagedHooksOnly` is what decides which hooks run."

**Fix:** Reword both claims.

### L5. `excludedCommands` limit (`README:62`) names only `~/.claude/settings.json`

settings-reference.md: "Entries in managed settings, `--settings`, and your `~/.claude/settings.json` still apply". The `--settings` source is missing from the README.

### L6. The review template's "Components" row omits plugin parts that run outside the sandbox

**Where:** `reviews/example-formatter.md:14`; `requiredMinimumVersion` 2.1.285.

The row lacks monitors, LSP servers, `bin/` executables and agents. Monitors and LSP servers run "with your full access" (sandboxing.md, "What runs outside the sandbox").

settings-reference.md says `allowManagedHooksOnly` blocks monitors of plugins that are not force-enabled only from "Claude Code v2.1.310 or later". That version is above the 2.1.285 floor.

**Fix:** Add these rows to the template. Raise the floor to 2.1.310, or state the gap.

### L7. Two plugin-customisation consequences are not stated (`README:107`)

- `strictKnownMarketplaces` without `{"source":"skills-dir"}` makes skills-directory plugins under `.claude/skills/*/.claude-plugin/` stop loading (plugins/org.md L236). This is an unstated cost; plain `SKILL.md` files are unaffected.
- The reason for not setting `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` covers only project `.claude/`. It does not cover user `~/.claude/agents` and `~/.claude/skills`. README-hipaa says to keep that key if `disableAutoMode` is set, and `disableAutoMode` is D1's fallback.

**Fix:** Note both.

### L8. `aurora-deletion-protection` has no documented exception path

**Where:** `policies.ts:97-104`.

Retiring a prod cluster requires first applying `deletionProtection: false`, and this mandatory policy blocks that deploy.

**Fix:** Document an exception route, such as a policy config exclusion through an L3 PR.

---

## Verdict

## MEDIUM

### M1. Phase 2 drops the template's `autoMode` `"$defaults"` pins, and the README gives a wrong reason

**Where:** `managed-settings.phase2.json:10-12`; `README.md:109` ("Unset is the default; only `classifyAllShell: true` is kept").

**Evidence:**
- README-hipaa.md ("Auto mode"): "The file pins `"$defaults"` in `environment`, `soft_deny`, and `hard_deny`, so a developer's own list adds to the built-in entries and can't replace them."
- auto-mode-config.md L74: "can't remove entries that managed settings provide".
- auto-mode-config.md L267–270: "Setting any of … `soft_deny`, or `hard_deny` without `"$defaults"` replaces the entire default list … `soft_deny`: every built-in soft block rule, including force push, `curl | bash`, production deploys … `hard_deny`: the built-in data exfiltration rule".
- Mutation: `autoMode.hard_deny: []` → the tests still pass.

**Effect:** With the pins unset, a `soft_deny`/`hard_deny` list in a developer's `~/.claude/settings.json` or `--settings` throws away the built-in rules. That includes the exfiltration rule. Auto mode stays available (D1), and in auto mode the classifier is often the only gate. The deviation is presented as a no-op, but it removes a lock.

**Fix:** Keep the three pins exactly as the template has them. This costs nothing. Add a test that each list contains `"$defaults"`. Alternatively, record it as a real deviation and state its effect.

### M2. `pulumi *` and `serverless *` exclusions reopen every credential the sandbox hides; the README says "each one prompts"

**Where:**
- `managed-settings.phase2.json:135-139`
- `README.md:62` ("excluded (they prompt)")
- `README.md:308-312` (finding 20)
- `README.md:322` ("so each one prompts")
- `tests/test_claude_settings.py:203-204`

**Evidence:**
- sandboxing.md, `excludedCommands` warning: "If you write a pattern that covers an interpreter, a script inside your working directory, or a tool that acts on a file there, as `docker compose` does with its compose file, Claude can write that file and then run it outside the sandbox."
- sandboxing.md: "An excluded command goes through the regular permission flow: … In auto mode, the classifier reviews other excluded commands."

**Effect:** OD12 auto-allows sandboxed commands, so a sandboxed command can write `index.ts` or `serverless.yml` in the repo with no prompt. `pulumi preview` then runs that code outside the sandbox: it can read `~/.config/gh`, `~/.ssh` and `~/.aws`, and the network is unrestricted.
- In Manual mode, the only prompt says `pulumi preview`.
- In auto mode, the classifier decides and nobody is asked.

So finding 20's claim (hiding `~/.config/gh` stops the agent approving PRs as the engineer) and the test comment are overstated, and "each one prompts" is wrong for auto mode. Framework layer 2 L211–222 already accepts this risk for `~/.aws`, but the E8 row, finding 20 and finding 22 do not carry it over.

**Fix:**
- State this limit in E8 "does not prove", finding 20 and finding 22.
- Fix "each one prompts" to "prompts in Manual mode; in auto mode the classifier decides".
- Option, with cost: add `permissions.ask: ["WebFetch", "Bash(aws *)", "Bash(pulumi *)", "Bash(serverless *)"]`. permission-modes.md L329 says "Explicit ask rules still force a prompt" in auto mode, so a person approves every unsandboxed run. The cost is a prompt per `aws` call in auto mode too.

### M3. The phase-2 sandbox read scope is a denylist; `allowManagedReadPathsOnly` does nothing here and would cancel `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories`

**Where:** `managed-settings.phase2.json:140-166` and `318-329`; `README.md:112` and `308`.

**Evidence:**
- sandboxing.md: by default sandboxed reads cover "Most of the machine".
- settings-reference.md L1541ff: `allowManagedReadPathsOnly` only filters `allowRead`. The docs' example pairs it with `"denyRead": ["~/"]` and `"allowRead": ["~/work"]`. Phase 2 sets neither, so the key has no effect.
- settings-reference.md L1083–1085: the sandbox half of `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` "doesn't reach sandboxed commands" when "`allowManagedReadPathsOnly` is set". Finding 19 proposes that key, so adopting it later would silently do nothing for sandboxed commands.
- Egress, sandboxing.md "Security limitations": "Allowing broad domains such as `github.com` can create paths for data exfiltration … domain fronting".
- Egress, README-hipaa.md: "a sandboxed command can send data to any allowlisted host, including other repositories on the same Git host".
- Mutation: adding `"*"` or `"*.amazonaws.com"` to `allowedDomains` → the tests still pass.

**Effect:** Sandboxed commands can read everything in home that is not on the list, with no prompt, and send it to `github.com`, npm or PyPI, for example a push to another repository using a token the attacker supplies. Credentials in Papaya's stack that the list misses (⚠️ paths not checked):
- Serverless Framework v4: `~/.serverlessrc` and `SERVERLESS_ACCESS_KEY`
- `PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE`
- key files that `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` or `KUBECONFIG` point to outside the denied folders
- Linear and Slack tokens

So "credential denies for the whole stack" (README:62) is overstated. None of this is stated in E8.

**Fix:**
- Either use the docs' pattern `denyRead: ["~/"]` plus `allowRead` for the workspace roots (cost: Papaya must fix where repos live, e.g. `~/src`), or drop `allowManagedReadPathsOnly` if `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` is preferred.
- State the egress-through-allowed-domains limit in E8.
- Add a test that `allowedDomains` contains no `*` entry.

### M4. Settings that break normal engineering work, with the cost not stated

**Where:** `README.md:114-117` (the costs paragraph names only `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`, `allowLocalBinding`, `cleanupPeriodDays` and `gh`); `SKILL.md:11-12`.

**Evidence:**
- README-hipaa.md, "What developers lose": private npm registries fail, `/goal` is gone under `allowManagedHooksOnly`.
- README-hipaa.md, "Check a computer" step 3: "`git` against a private repository can still fail to sign in, because the file hides SSH keys, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.netrc`, the GitHub token variables, and the `gh` configuration".
- sandboxing.md: git over SSH fails on macOS; Go CLIs fail TLS on macOS; Unix sockets such as Docker's are not allowed (`allowAllUnixSockets: false`).
- settings-reference.md: `allowLocalBinding: false` also blocks connecting to servers on localhost on macOS.
- sandboxing.md L13: the sandbox does not run on native Windows, so with `failIfUnavailable` Claude Code does not start there.

**Effect:** Inside the sandbox, `git fetch`, `git pull` and `git push` to the private monorepo fail, as do private-scope `npm ci`, Docker and Testcontainers, and local database tests on macOS. The prod-change skill tells the agent to "open a pull request", but it can neither push nor run `gh` from the sandbox.

**Fix:** List these in the costs paragraph, with the workaround (`!` prompt). Note the native-Windows effect.

### M5. The wildcard rule can be evaded with `?` forms that mean the same as `*` or `<service>:*`

**Where:** `pulumi-policy/policies.ts:31-43`.

**Evidence (probe output):**
- `"s3:?*"` → `[]`
- `"ec2:**"` → `[]`
- `"*?"` → `[]`
- `"iam:?*"` → flagged, because only identity services are checked for any wildcard

IAM supports `?` in action names (⚠️ from memory; the IAM doc was not fetched). Under that reading, `s3:?*` grants every S3 action.

**Effect:** A mandatory policy meant to compensate for OD8 is passed by an equivalent spelling.

**Fix:** Treat an action as a full wildcard when the whole action, or the part after `:`, matches `^[*?]+$`. Add the three cases above to the tests.
